summary: A Pacific Mining Watch news article reports that Mayur Resources Ltd describes its Orokolo Bay iron sands project in Papua New Guinea's Gulf as simple, low-capex and financially robust, with multiple product revenue streams. Citing a definitive feasibility study, it gives a post-tax NPV of US$131 million and an IRR of 103.7 per cent, along with planned production of titano-magnetite, construction sand and zircon-rich concentrate. The article also summarises site works, offtake talks, the environmental permit, and the Amazon Bay exploration project's vanadium, titanium and iron potential.
one_line: Mayur Resources reports its Orokolo Bay iron sands project in PNG is financially robust, with a US$131 million NPV and 103.7% IRR.
key_facts: The Orokolo Bay iron sands project in Papua New Guinea's Gulf is described by Mayur Resources Ltd as simple, low-capital expenditure (capex) and financially robust.
Mayur Resources' iron and industrial sands portfolio in PNG is held by Mayur Iron.
According to a definitive feasibility study (DFS), the project would produce a post-tax (real) net present value of US$131 million (about K459.8 million) at a 10 per cent discount rate.
The project's internal rate of return (IRR) is 103.7 per cent.
The operational design calls for an initial capex of US$20.5 million (about K71.9 million).
The planned near surface mining operation is forecast to produce 0.5mtpa of titano-magnetite, 1mtpa of construction sand and up to 10ktpa of zircon-rich heavy mineral concentrate.
Site enabling works have begun in Orokolo Bay, and off-take discussions remain ongoing with a focus on high value magnetite for the Asian market.
A 25-year environmental permit issued by the Conservation Environment Protection Authority was in place for Orokolo Bay.
The proposed post-mining sustainability land use initiative is a mechanised sago plantation, expected to leave a lasting positive legacy for local landowners.
The Amazon Bay in Central project has significant potential for three high value product streams: vanadium, titanium and iron.
Mayur Resources describes Amazon Bay as an advanced exploration project that brings development synergies with Orokolo Bay.
Previous exploration focused on Amazon Bay as a magnetite resource without fully pursuing its titanium and significant vanadium potential.
Mayur Resources released its annual report the week before the article was published on 04 November.
